questions.q: Why can't Sales.SalesReason be added to dw.FactProductSales as a simple SalesReasonKey foreign key column, the way the other four dimensions were added?
options: Because Sales.SalesReason doesn't actually exist in AdventureWorks2012
Because a single order can have more than one sales reason attached at once, making it a many-to-many relationship a single column can't represent
Because SalesReasonID is a text column, not an integer
Because the fact table already has the maximum number of foreign keys allowed
questions.explain: A single column can only hold one value per row. Since an order can legitimately have multiple sales reasons, a single FK column would have to arbitrarily discard all but one.

questions.q: What is dw.BridgeOrderSalesReason, and how does it connect to dw.FactProductSales?
options: A new column directly on dw.FactProductSales
A table of SalesOrderID/SalesReasonKey pairs that joins to the fact table through SalesOrderID, the existing degenerate dimension
A view that replaces dw.FactProductSales entirely
A copy of dw.DimSalesReason with no additional structure
questions.explain: The bridge table holds key pairs and joins to the fact table through the SalesOrderID degenerate dimension already kept on dw.FactProductSales — no new column is added to the fact table itself.

questions.q: Why can a query joining dw.FactProductSales through dw.BridgeOrderSalesReason legitimately return more rows than dw.FactProductSales itself has?
options: This indicates a bug in the bridge table and should never happen
Because an order with multiple sales reasons fans out to multiple rows in the join, which is expected and correct for a many-to-many bridge
Because dw.FactProductSales has duplicate rows
Because the bridge table double-counts every order automatically
questions.explain: Fan-out is expected when joining through a bridge table — an order with two reasons produces two joined rows. Any aggregation using this join has to account for that.

questions.q: What does nothing changing about dw.FactProductSales or its original four dimensions during this schema change demonstrate?
options: That the change is additive — every query, report, or model already built against this warehouse keeps working unmodified
That the bridge table pattern is only cosmetic and has no real effect
That dw.DimSalesReason is optional and can be skipped
That the original fact table design was wrong and needs to be rebuilt
questions.explain: Because dw.DimSalesReason and dw.BridgeOrderSalesReason are entirely new objects, nothing that already depends on the existing fact table or dimensions is affected.

questions.q: What real AdventureWorks2012 table proves that orders can have more than one sales reason, and how?
options: Sales.SalesOrderHeader, by checking its TotalDue column
Sales.SalesOrderHeaderSalesReason, by grouping on SalesOrderID and finding groups with COUNT(*) > 1
Production.Product, by checking ProductSubcategoryID
Sales.Customer, by checking PersonID and StoreID
questions.explain: Grouping Sales.SalesOrderHeaderSalesReason by SalesOrderID and filtering for COUNT(*) > 1 surfaces real orders with multiple reasons attached, proving the many-to-many relationship with real data.
